public_upstream.fix_subject: Apply the buffered IV on the AES-OCB EVP_Cipher() path

oh_source.equivalence: cipher_aes_ocb.c differs from upstream 3.0.9 by 5 lines (OH-own in==NULL Final handling); vulnerable one-shot path identical
oh_source.l4_evidence: aes_ocb_cipher (cipher_aes_ocb.c:497) lacks the key_set/update_iv head check; narrow patch (source-file part of upstream diff) applies clean

vulnerability.summary: AES-OCB one-shot EVP_Cipher() path never flushes the buffered IV; when it is the first data operation, the effective OCB nonce is 0 regardless of the caller's IV — catastrophic nonce reuse under the same key, silent at the API level.
vulnerability.trigger: EVP_Cipher() as the first data operation on an AES-OCB context (no prior streaming call)
vulnerability.verification_level: runtime-verified 2x2 matrix (2026-09-23, WSL2 clang, OH checkout static build): S1 (no AAD, body one-shot vs streaming) orig -> ct=DIFF tag=DIFF exit 1 (direct observation of nonce-0 encryption); S2 (AAD streaming + body one-shot) orig -> SAME (streaming AAD already flushed the IV — corroborates mechanism); patched -> both SAME, S2 unchanged (no regression)
vulnerability.crypto_note: first cryptographic-class case in the series; verified by ciphertext/tag semantic equivalence, no memory observation needed

controls.name: aad-streaming-first
controls.desc: S2 shape: one-shot body after streaming AAD behaves correctly on both builds (IV flushed by the streaming call)
